1. The buttons are cool, but need some work. Whether or not it was intentional, I like the resemblance of the buttons to Microsoft Office. The hover-color looks washed out, though. My suggestion is to increase the color contrast to balance the lightening.

  2. The heading ribbons on the sidebar do not match the buttons. I like the button colors, so I'd suggest recoloring the ribbons to match.

  3. Hover underlines should be underlines, not borders. With some exceptions, text hover-effects should be underlined with text decoration and not borders because borders work with the box around the text rather than with the text. It has some unintended side effects that are distracting.

    However, in some places, like the account information in the top-right corner, it looks nice.

  4. Box shadows are rough and distracting. I think you should make them more subtle.

  5. The markdown section in the sidebar should be the same color as the sidebar. It looks a little odd.

  6. The dotted hyperlink effects in the sidebar should be restricted to the markdown section. I like the decoration, but it looks weird when used on message the moderators, InfiniteSpaces, etc. below the markdown section.

  7. The box bottom-border on the page name next to the tab menu looks weird. I think it should be omitted from the underline.

  8. The tab menu's 'Hot' does not have a hover effect. Perhaps you forgot about it.

  9. Button text contrasts too much with the buttons.

  10. The sidebar heading ribbons should be widened to stretch around the sidebar rather than just the markdown section.

That's all of the issues I see with the theme thus far. I encourage you to continue your good work because I like it so far.

Scientists Find Area Of The Brain That Motivates Us To Exercise

From the article: "Turner and colleagues turned to mice genetically engineered to block signals from the dorsal medial habenula. Compared to normal mice who love to run on wheels (even in the wild), these mouse models were lethargic and ran far less. “Without a functioning dorsal medial habenula, the mice became couch potatoes,” Turner explains in a news release. “They were physically capable of running but appeared unmotivated to do it.”

These mice also didn’t prefer sweetened drinking water over regular water. The lack of motivation to exercise or even seek pleasure is a mouse model for depression -- and in this case, they just didn’t care, KPLU explains."

Fascinating stuff. I wonder (and they didn't ask) if exercising despite being unmotivated can stimulate that region of the brain and cause you to enjoy it after awhile. I know that I didn't want to exercise at all, and when I started making myself go, I started to enjoy it. The longer I stick with it, the more rewarding it is.

Not proof by any means, but having struggled with trying to stay motivated to exercise myself, I can say that exercising more does (to some extent) motivate me to do it more. However, the second I decide to 'take a break' that break ends up killing all motivation to exercise any more. It's tough.
